- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and model forecasts a sharp rise, check for overshoot: if true outcome drops within 3–5 days, cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts a decline, avoid underestimating — model often misses bottoming; add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) — if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, cap forecast rise to 3–4% max.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean — apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is high and price is trending up, model often forecasts too high — reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment >0.75 and price >75.00.
- If sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often forecasts too low — add 2–4% to forecast if sentiment <0.33 and price <70.00.
